card: Bitcoin Core ignores BIP35 mempool messages from peers that have transaction relay disabled, unless explicitly granted the mempool permission. Currently, an inbound peer can connect with fRelay=false to bypass the node's inbound transaction-relay capacity limits while still requesting full mempool inventory. This closes a loophole introduced with the inbound transaction-relay capacity enforcement in PR #28463 while preserving SPV clients that issue BIP37 filterload before requesting mempool contents.
evidence: PR description: 'When a node offers NODE_BLOOM, an inbound peer can advertise fRelay=false and request BIP35 mempool inventory while remaining outside the inbound transaction-relay capacity introduced in #28463.'
problem: When a node offers NODE_BLOOM, an inbound peer can advertise fRelay=false to avoid counting against the inbound transaction-relay capacity limit added in PR #28463, while still obtaining mempool transaction inventory through BIP35 mempool messages.
summary: Ignore BIP35 mempool requests from inbound peers that have transaction relay disabled (such as fRelay=false), unless the peer has the mempool net permission. Peers using BIP37 filterload turn on transaction relay and are thereby subjected to existing inbound transaction-relay capacity limits.
